content:
Heaps Normal is an Australian non-alc beer company whilst Four Loko is known for its RTDs. Image supplied

Casella Family Brands (CFB), home of Yellow Tail, has announced two new non-wine partnerships with Heaps Normal and Four Loko in Australia, effective 3 August 2026.

The company said the new agreements “further strengthen CFB’s position as a leading diversified beverage company, expanding its presence cross key growth categories and reinforcing its commitment to evolving consumer trends”.

CFB has entered into a distribution partnership with Heaps Normal, a non-alc beer brand. CFB will manage distribution across New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Queensland. The agreement excludes draught and keg formats, which will continue to be managed by Heaps Normal.

“Ours is an industry built on quality time with your people, and that’s never mattered more,” said Andy Miller, co-founder and CEO of Heaps Normal.

“Our friends at Casella Family Brands have a deep personal connection to the trade we all love, and we can’t imagine a better crew to help Heaps Normal on its mission to throw a better party.”

Meanwhile, under a new long-term agreement with Four Loko, CFB will manufacture and distribute the brand in Australia.

Founded by Phusion Projects in the United States, Four Loko celebrates its 21st anniversary this year.

CFB said the brand has built a “strong global reputation in the ready-to-drink (RTD) category through distinctive flavours and a focus on innovation, with an established presence across North America, South America and Europe”.

The partnership will see the launch of a vodka-based RTD in three flavours at 7% ABV, alongside the introduction of a 440mL single-serve can format “tailored to Australian consumers”.

Jeff Wright, co-founder of Phusion Projects, said Four Loko is incredibly excited to be partnering with Casella.

“Their manufacturing expertise and distribution strength make them an ideal partner to support Four Loko’s continued growth in Australia.”

Together, CFB and Four Loko will focus on strengthening availability, supporting retail partners, and expanding consumer engagement across Australia.

Casella Family Brands general manager of sales, Chris Blockley, said that the partnerships “highlight CFB’s ability to partner with leading brands and execute across diverse categories”.

“Our state-of-the-art production facility and end-to-end expertise enable us to partner with globally recognised brands that lead their categories. These partnerships reflect a deliberate strategy to focus where we can make the greatest impact, using our scale and customer relationships to build stronger brands.

“Together, these brands complement our wine portfolio and expand our relevance across more consumers and occasions, creating a portfolio that meets evolving consumer needs and is well positioned for future growth,” Blockley said.

title: St Hugo becomes first-ever wine partner for Thredbo Alpine Resort
summary:
Vinarchy’s St Hugo brand has teamed up with Thredbo Resort in NSW as the destination’s first-ever wine partner. St Hugo will be the official wine partner of the resort for the 2026 winter season, delivering a series of “elevated wine, dining and hospitality experiences across the mountain”. "There are few destinations in Australia as iconic as Thredbo, making it the perfect setting for St Hugo's first alpine partnership,” said Amy Davill, Vinarchy APAC marketing director. “As the first wine brand to partner with the resort, we're excited to bring together exceptional wine, dining and hospitality through a series of experiences that celebrate the best of the Australian snow season."

The post St Hugo becomes first-ever wine partner for Thredbo Alpine Resort appeared first on Winetitles.
content:
St Hugo will host a calendar of events as part of the partnership. Image supplied

Vinarchy’s St Hugo brand has teamed up with Thredbo Resort in NSW as the destination’s first-ever wine partner.

St Hugo will be the official wine partner of the resort for the 2026 winter season, delivering a series of “elevated wine, dining and hospitality experiences across the mountain”.

“There are few destinations in Australia as iconic as Thredbo, making it the perfect setting for St Hugo’s first alpine partnership,” said Amy Davill, Vinarchy APAC marketing director.

“As the first wine brand to partner with the resort, we’re excited to bring together exceptional wine, dining and hospitality through a series of experiences that celebrate the best of the Australian snow season.”

St Hugo becomes the first-ever presenting partner of the “iconic Kareela Snowcat Dinners” – one of Australia’s “most unique alpine dining experiences”. Accessible only via a snowcat journey through the snow-covered mountains, the experience pairs “exceptional food, fine wine and breathtaking views high above the resort”.

Throughout the season, guests will also be able to enjoy St Hugo wines across Thredbo’s venues, including Cascades, Kareela Hutte and the Lounge Bar.

A calendar of events is planned for the partnership, including the St Hugo Sessions at Kareela Hutte taking place from Friday 21 August to Sunday 23 August. The event will feature a DJ and “an elevated après-ski atmosphere set against the backdrop of the Snowy Mountains”.

Thredbo partnerships and MTB business manager, Tim Windshuttle, said that the resort is delighted to welcome St Hugo as its first-ever wine partner.

“From the Kareela Hutte Snowcat Dinners to the St Hugo Sessions and exclusive hospitality experiences throughout the season, this partnership adds an exciting new dimension to the Thredbo experience.

“The partnership brings together two iconic Australian brands, setting a new benchmark for luxury hospitality in the mountains,” Windshuttle said.

St Hugo will also host the inaugural St Hugo Chalet Experience, an “invitation-only alpine residence where guests will be immersed in the world of St Hugo through a curated program of wine, culinary and alpine experiences”. According to the winery, the experience is designed exclusively for the season and will offer “a unique way to experience St Hugo within Australia’s premier snow destination”.

“For generations, alpine destinations around the world have been synonymous with luxury travel, great food and unforgettable hospitality. Together, St Hugo and Thredbo are bringing that spirit to Australia’s snowfields in a fresh and distinctly local way,” added Davill.

Thredbo Resort has been named ‘Australia’s Best Ski Resort’ for nine consecutive years.

content:
VineHealth Australia is inviting South Australians to nominate for the 2026 VineHealth Biosecurity Champion Award, with entries closing this Friday 7 August.

The award “celebrates individuals who demonstrate outstanding commitment, leadership and innovation in biosecurity” with entries open to those who work in the South Australian wine industry.

This may include, but is not limited to:

  • South Australian vineyard owners
  • South Australian winemakers
  • South Australian regional associations
  • South Australian tourism and cellar door operators
  • Contributors to the South Australian wine industry (e.g. consultants, researchers, viticulturists)

Anyone who knows of or is a biosecurity champion, such as a vineyard owner who goes “above and beyond” to protect the industry from biosecurity threats, is encouraged to nominate using the form here.

The winner will be announced at the South Australian Wine Industry Dinner on Thursday 17 September 2026.

The 2026 Len Evans Tutorial (LET) board has announced the 12 Australian wine professionals who will be the participants in the 24th tutorial, to be held from 2 – 6 November 2026 at Spicer’s Guesthouse in the Hunter Valley.

The 12 successful scholars will join more than 270 tutorial alumni “to receive invaluable training and education designed to elevate their contribution to the Australian wine show system, nurture future industry leaders and develop better all-round wine professionals”.

Organisers say this was Len Evans’ vision and the legacy of the LET, with the five residential days often dubbed ‘the greatest wine school in the world’.

Last year’s dux, Andrew Bretherton, head winemaker at WA’s Juniper Estate, said the experience was the greatest wine week of his life.

“193 applications were received this year, a record, with women making up two thirds of this year’s final Scholar list, the highest ever,” said Sally Evans, chair of the LET board.

“The selection panel continues to be overwhelmed by the quality and volume of applications. It’s a privilege to read each one, and we often follow the career progress of applicants over several years. As we can only welcome 12 scholars annually, persistence — sometimes across multiple applications — is often what it takes.”

The program for the 2026 Australian Women in Wine Symposium has been revealed, with this year’s symposium titled ‘Rising Together – Shaping What Comes Next’.

  • Industry – navigating change and shaping the future of Australian wine

“The symposium is more than an event…it’s an opportunity to connect with a national network of women and allies, celebrate progress and contribute to the future of our industry,” said organisers.

title: William Wilson receives RAS Contributor Award for dedication to Sydney Royal Wine Show
summary:
The Royal Agricultural Society of NSW has announced William Wilson as the recipient of its RAS Contributor Award, recognising his “unwavering dedication and service to the Sydney Royal Wine Show”. The Royal Agricultural Society of NSW said Wilson has been an integral part of the Sydney Royal Wine Show and Sydney Royal Beer & Cider Show since 2012. “In his roles as steward and now chief steward, he has gone above and beyond to improve the competition, mentor others and ensure every show is conducted to the highest standard,” the organisation explained.

The post William Wilson receives RAS Contributor Award for dedication to Sydney Royal Wine Show appeared first on Winetitles.
content:
L–R: Dr Sam Walker, Lyndey Milan OAM, William Wilson, Sally Evans and Angus Barnes. Image supplied

The Royal Agricultural Society of NSW has announced William Wilson as the recipient of its RAS Contributor Award, recognising his “unwavering dedication and service to the Sydney Royal Wine Show”.

The Royal Agricultural Society of NSW said Wilson has been an integral part of the Sydney Royal Wine Show and Sydney Royal Beer & Cider Show since 2012.

“In his roles as steward and now chief steward, he has gone above and beyond to improve the competition, mentor others and ensure every show is conducted to the highest standard,” the organisation explained.

Beyond the Sydney Royal competitions, Wilson has made an “outstanding contribution to the NSW wine industry through his role at the International Convention Centre Sydney, where he is committed to showcasing NSW wines”.

Wilson was among Australia’s first certified sommeliers through the Court of Master Sommeliers.

“William’s professionalism, generosity, attention to detail and quiet leadership have earned the respect and friendship of everyone who has had the pleasure of working with him,” RAS President John Bennett said.

“He is an integral part of the Sydney Royal Wine Show team, and his dedication has played a significant role in advancing the competition and ensuring its continued success.”

The award was presented to Wilson by Bennett at an event on Monday night and coincides with the 200-year celebration of the Sydney Royal Wine Show, which first awarded a medal for ‘colonial’ wine in 1826.

The organisation said that today, Wilson and the Sydney Royal Wine Show team continue to uphold the shows legacy and “support the ongoing success of one of Australia’s most respected wine competitions”.

Established in 1988, the RAS Contributor Award recognises an individual’s outstanding contribution to the RAS and the wider agricultural industry. Only one award is presented each year, with recipients selected from across all RAS competitions and sections.

content:
The board has welcomed Anishka Jelicich’s commencement. Image supplied

New Zealand Winegrowers (NZW) has today announced that Anishka Jelicich has commenced her role as Chief Executive Officer.

She joins the organisation following “a successful international career spanning more than two decades across New Zealand, the United Kingdom and Europe”.

Jelicich said she has had the privilege of seeing New Zealand wine through the eyes of the world during her time working internationally in the global wine and drinks sector.

“Time and again I’ve seen the extraordinary respect our wines, our people and our industry command globally. That perspective has only deepened a connection that is both personal and professional, making it a real privilege to join an organisation that has helped shape one of New Zealand’s great success stories through the leadership of Philip Gregan (recently retired CEO), the NZW board, the NZW team, our members and those who have contributed over many years.

“Today, New Zealand wine is the country’s eighth largest export, generating approximately NZ$2.1 billion annually, with our distinctive, refreshing and sustainable wines enjoyed by consumers in more than 100 markets around the world. My first priority is therefore to listen, learn and spend time with people across the industry, understanding what matters most before we write the next chapter together.”

Chair of New Zealand Winegrowers, Fabian Yukich, said the board is delighted to welcome Jelicich into the role.

“We are very pleased to have Anishka join us as CEO. She brings a deep understanding of the New Zealand wine industry, combined with extensive global experience and strong leadership capability. Her strategic perspective and ability to build alignment across stakeholders will be invaluable as we navigate both the opportunities and challenges ahead for our sector,” Yukich said.

NZW said Jelicich’s appointment comes at an important time for the New Zealand wine industry, with “continued global demand for premium New Zealand wines” making the sector “well positioned for long-term growth” and also to respond to “a range of global and domestic pressures facing growers and winemakers”.

The Winetitles Great Australian Grenache, Shiraz, Mourvèdre/Mataro (GSM) Challenge has announced the 2026 judging line up and sponsors.

Event director Juliam McLean revealed that Jen Pfeiffer will return as chair for the challenge and will be joined by judges Liz Heidenreich, Katie Spain, Tyson Bitter, Steve Paul and Justin Purser.

Fowles Wines will again host this year’s event, with entries opening online Monday 3 August and closing Friday 4 September. Judging will take place over three days from Tuesday 29 September to Thursday 1 October and winners will be announced online Monday 2 November.

title: Cooks Lot releases handpicked 2025 vintage Chardonnay and Pinot Noir
summary:
Cooks Lot has released its 2025 vintage Orange region Cooks Lot ‘Handpicked’ Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. Owner and winemaker Duncan Cook said that, while hand harvesting is more labour-intensive, it is “definitely more selective”. "Our vintage team take a great deal of care working their way through the vineyard, picking each bunch by hand, carefully selecting the best and leaving those bunches that may be damaged or not quite ripe. The result is a higher degree of flavour concentration and balance in the finished wines. It is more expensive, but years of experience have shown the quality speaks for itself.”

The post Cooks Lot releases handpicked 2025 vintage Chardonnay and Pinot Noir appeared first on Winetitles.
content:
The grapes for the wines have been handpicked and each bottle retails for RRP $35. Image supplied

Cooks Lot has released its 2025 vintage Orange region Cooks Lot ‘Handpicked’ Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

Owner and winemaker Duncan Cook said that, while hand harvesting is more labour-intensive, it is “definitely more selective”.

“Our vintage team take a great deal of care working their way through the vineyard, picking each bunch by hand, carefully selecting the best and leaving those bunches that may be damaged or not quite ripe. The result is a higher degree of flavour concentration and balance in the finished wines. It is more expensive, but years of experience have shown the quality speaks for itself.

“In the winery, our ‘Handpicked’ wines are crafted with complexity in mind. The wines see more new oak and extended maturation. The objective is to produce wines that showcase the region’s fruit purity, with greater depth, length, texture and complexity upon release, while also offering longevity in the cellar.

“We aim to create a more layered palate, enhanced structure, and a higher level of refinement than the ‘Allotment’ range.

“After many years in the kitchen championing fresh produce and proteins, winemaking shares many aspects. My underlying challenge is to hero the variety and the region with the finished wine. Using various winemaking techniques, including barrel selection and maturation time, should create the pedestal and hone the focus that ensures they shine.

The 2025 Cooks Lot ‘Handpicked’ Chardonnay is barrel fermented with partial solids “to build complexity and texture, balancing the lovely concentration and varietal expression of the Orange region fruit”. Cooks Lot said it is aged on its lees, with regular stirring, in a combination of new and one-year-old French oak barriques.

The 2025 Cooks Lot ‘Handpicked’ Pinot Noir is made from a combination of MV6 and 777 clones grown in vineyards sitting at an average elevation above 900m.

“The Pinot Noir was fermented in small open fermenters, with a small component as whole bunches, by wild yeast and gently hand plunged four times a day. This is gentle on the skins, while building complexity and flavour extraction. It also allows us to carefully monitor the ferment,” said Cook.

The free-run juice and pressings were “barrelled separately and matured in tightly grained French oak puncheons for 12 months, prior to blending and bottling”.

Retailing for RRP $35 each, the wines are available here via the Cooks Lot website.

The post Great Australian Shiraz Challenge reveals judging panel and sponsors for 2026 appeared first on Winetitles.
content:
The Great Australian Shiraz Challenge has revealed its 2026 judging line-up and challenge sponsors.

“We are delighted to have Jen Pfeiffer returning as chair, she will be joined by Liz Heidenreich, Katie Spain, Tyson Bitter, Steve Paul and Justin Purser,” said event director Julian McLean.

Fowles Wines will again host this year’s event, with entries opening online Monday 3 August and closing Friday 4 September.

Judging will take place over three days from Tuesday 29 September to Thursday 1 October and winners will be announced online Monday 2 November.

Organisers said that the challenge is a “unique opportunity for Australia’s premier red winemakers to showcase their Shiraz, benchmark winemaking and regional points of differences and assist with reinforcing the reputation of the variety as a national and international wine icon”.

The challenge has been going for 32 years, with wines “classed and tasted based on climate and regional points of difference”. Organisers say this helps ensure all entries are “judged fairly and objectively”.

The award categories have expanded over the competition’s years of operating. In 2016, individual state-based trophies and the award for ‘Best Shiraz Over 5 Years Old’ were introduced. In 2021, the ‘Best Organic Shiraz Trophy’ acknowledged winemakers’ commitment to the category, and a ‘Best Sparkling Shiraz’ class was even introduced in 2022.

Saint Martin Oak returns as the naming rights sponsor, with support also from Orora Glass, MCC Label Solutions, Winetitles Media, Sanector, Melbourne Royal and Interpack.

More information can be found here or by contacting event director Julian McLean at shirazchallenge@gmail.com.
